candidates.hypothesis: Conditional overnight drift ('buy the dip'): after a US close with net selling (closing relative signed volume RSV < 0, 15:15-16:15 ET), go long equity index futures 01:30-03:30 ET as European (and Tokyo) participants arrive and dealers offload inventory
candidates.mechanism: dealer inventory risk: closing order imbalance absorbed by market makers is offloaded when overseas participants arrive (European open); reversal larger after sell-offs
candidates.best_source: Boyarchenko, Larsen, Whelan, The Overnight Drift, FRBNY Staff Report 917 (rev. Aug 2022); RFS 36(9) 2023
candidates.post_2015_or_oos: in-sample to 2020; authors' 2021-2025 update shows decay (unconditional ~0; imbalance link 'much narrower')
candidates.published_effect: BtD mean 6.07% annualized before costs, 4.04% after bid-ask; Sharpe 1.78 / 1.10; holds on ~50% of trading days
candidates.dispersion: Sharpe 1.78 gross (annual sd 2.95% on the strategy's daily series), 1.10 after spread
candidates.quote: We also consider a conditional trading strategy that 'buys-the-dip', denoted BtD, which holds the e-mini during the OD+ period but only on trading days following a negative order flow at market close (RSV close t-1 < 0).
